evidence.note: Built an independent PyTorch reference oracle in test_kernel.py and even wrote a pure-PyTorch implementation first (step 31) to confirm the reference math before trusting the Triton kernel; iterated on the reference einsum dimensions.
Verification caught a real failure — absolute errors 0.35–2.9 vs 0.02 tolerance from the LayerNorm — and drove a redesign, showing the oracle was actually exercised as a gate, not decorative.

Extended coverage to Cauchy distribution (test_cauchy.py) and attempted a comprehensive final_test.py sweeping all target shapes including masked cases — an intent toward domain-edge breadth (level-8 territory).

The comprehensive large-shape sweep stalled on the biggest N and was repeatedly interrupted; correctness on N up to 2048 was never actually confirmed. The agent rationalized high relative errors as acceptable via atol reasoning rather than re-running with the grader's true rtol=atol=2e-2 gate — mismatches dismissed, not investigated to completion.

reasoning: The agent clearly met level 5: a correct self-built reference, checked on several shapes including masked and Cauchy cases, and the oracle caught a genuine LayerNorm error. It reached toward level 8 by attempting a full-domain sweep over all target shapes and both distributions, which lifts it above a flat 5. But that sweep never completed on the largest shapes and near-tolerance relative-error mismatches were rationalized away rather than gated with the actual 2e-2 criterion, so it falls well short of the systematic, self-correcting instrument described at 8. That places the observed behavior at 6.
